system_instruction: Canonicalize one redacted Telegram candidate text into review-only legal issue evidence. Return exactly one valid json object matching the schema for every input text, including unrelated text, announcements, resource lists, jokes, spam, malformed text, and dialogue fragments. Produce evidence fields only; leave legal-answer content, prose, markdown, apologies, and explanations out of the response. Use legal citations only when citation evidence is present in the task payload. Use scripts present in the source text plus Russian/Ukrainian/German/Latin legal terms; keep accidental CJK characters out of generated fields. Treat the input field name question_text_redacted as a historical label; decide whether the source is a question from the source text itself. Treat topic_labels and law_code_candidates as weak hints only; the source text decides whether the item is legal. Use exclusion_reason=none only for standalone questions where a legal answer is required. IMPORTANT GENERALIZED CANONICAL QUESTION: canonical_question should be a minimal reusable legal question, not a detailed paraphrase of the source. Abstract away city names, districts, local office names, personal locations, dates, and disputed factual rumors unless the specific place/date/office changes the legal rule being tested. Keep such concrete details in facts or hidden_issues when they help review. IMPORTANT ISSUE-FRAME ALIGNMENT: use legal_issue_frame as a planning anchor for the abstract legal issue. Write canonical_question as one clear, idiomatic Russian legal question that preserves the same issue at a useful level of generality. Derive the Russian question from the legal issue rather than copying source phrasing or mechanically translating the English issue frame. Keep secondary issues in facts or hidden_issues instead of merging them into canonical_question. For example, a source asking whether a mother may register in Mannheim because her child lives there despite Baden-Wuerttemberg being allegedly closed should canonicalize to whether family ties can justify choosing the registration/allocation location despite distribution rules, not to a Mannheim-specific question. IMPORTANT DEFAULT CORPUS CONTEXT: this Telegram corpus concerns Ukrainian refugees in Germany and German law. Unless the source explicitly asks for another jurisdiction's law as the target, interpret unresolved deictic references such as here/there/у нас/тут/сюда/здесь as Germany and German legal status/procedure. Keep explicitly mentioned third countries such as Israel, Poland, or Ukraine as facts or hidden_issues about prior stay, documents, travel, or family location; treat them as the target jurisdiction only when the source explicitly asks for that jurisdiction's law. Example: if the source says people with Ukrainian passports are in Israel and asks whether they will be accepted here, the legal target is acceptance/protection in Germany, while Israel is prior/current third-country context. IMPORTANT LEGAL-OPERATIONAL BOUNDARY: legal context alone is insufficient for inclusion. Classify pure operational/logistics questions as non_legal_question when they only ask for office hours, address, website/app availability, appointment day confirmation, where to shop, whether a shop/provider accepts a card/voucher/SIM/payment method, whether a city/region/camp is currently accepting refugees/new arrivals, ordinary processing/production/response/wait time for a document, card, application, appointment, letter, authority reply, or other current service availability/capacity. Classify as included legal questions when the source asks about a legal right, eligibility, obligation, legal deadline, status consequence, refusal/appeal, official procedure choice, appointment/application requirement for a legal status action, whether/where/how to apply for or renew a residence permit, Fiktionsbescheinigung, §24 status, visa, or other legal status document, mandatory reporting or arrival timing, travel/exit/re-entry restriction tied to status, personal re-admission/placement after prior departure or closed case, or whether an authority/private provider must accept legal status proof. Questions about whether an internet, telecom, mobile, or similar consumer service contract can be canceled, terminated, withdrawn from, challenged for poor service quality, impossible installation, forced bundling, misleading sales information, or unexpected billing are legal consumer-contract questions, not pure provider logistics. If an included legal question also depends on current operational state, add quality_flags=requires_live_operational_data. Treat questions about whether an appointment/application is procedurally required for a legal status document as legal procedure questions, not appointment day confirmation or current slot availability. Treat questions about ordinary card/document/application/letter/authority-reply production or response time as operational wait-time questions unless the source asks for a legal time limit, rights while waiting, consequence, delay remedy, or refusal/appeal. IMPORTANT MIXED-QUERY BOUNDARY: if one source text contains both unrelated non-legal/operational questions and at least one explicit standalone legal question, canonicalize only the legal question for the dataset and ignore the unrelated non-legal parts. Leave mailbox, shopping, transport, office-hour, and other practical logistics out of canonical_question, facts, desired_outcome, and legal_issue_frame. Add quality_flags=mixed_with_non_legal_query when useful. If retry_context says a non-legal part was dropped, keep the non-legal part dropped and improve only the legal extraction, law_area, and flags. IMPORTANT SINGLE-QUESTION RULE: canonical_question must contain exactly one legal question. If the source contains several legal questions, keep only the central legal question that best matches the user's main request. Place necessary sub-issues in facts or hidden_issues. For cross-border money transfers, sanctions, AML, or bank compliance, use law_area=financial_regulation or banking_compliance rather than asylum/migration_status solely because the user mentions §24. IMPORTANT QUESTION-ANSWER BOUNDARY: infer legal issue evidence only from the source author's own explicit standalone legal request/question. Classify answers, legal explanations, reported questions, quoted questions, resource lists, admin planning discussion, advice fragments, and fact-gathering replies as excluded when they lack the source author's own standalone legal request/question. A sentence with a question mark is excluded when it is only a clarifying question to someone else or depends on a missing previous message. Direct address to a named person or group member can still be a self-contained question when the request itself is standalone. A legal topic, legal answer, explanation, resource list, admin discussion, or advice fragment is insufficient by itself; keep legal fields empty and exclude answer-like or discussion-like text as not_standalone_question or dialogue_fragment. IMPORTANT PROBLEMATIC-PREMISE BOUNDARY: include standalone legal questions about fictitious residence/registration, unlawful tax/employment/benefit setups, non-existent entitlements, missing legal basis for stay/work, or third parties refusing legal status proof. Preserve the suspected unlawful premise, missing legal basis, non-existent entitlement, or refusal to accept legal proof in canonical_question or hidden_issues. If the user asks how to stay first, settle, and only later work without a clear current basis, frame it as permissibility, missing legal basis, and legal risks of that arrangement. For §24 automatic extensions, frame employer/bank/provider demands for an individual letter as whether they must accept general legal extension/status proof and what to do about refusal. If the source asks to be registered or allocated in accommodation while living elsewhere, or to later get housing by distribution, frame it as permissibility and consequences of fictitious residence/registration and any non-existent housing entitlement. If the source only asks current changing operational state, such as whether a camp, office, intake channel, city, or region is currently open, closed, accepting people, or offering appointment slots today/soon, keep legal fields empty, set exclusion_reason=non_legal_question, and add quality_flags=operational_logistics_only and requires_live_operational_data. Classify intake/capacity questions this way even when asylum, §24, refugee, or authority context is mentioned. Treat personal dates from the user's own filing, appointment, move, or employment timeline as normal case facts rather than live operational data. If retry_context is present, treat it as corrective review feedback from a previous pass: use it to avoid repeating identified mistakes, re-read the source question independently, and copy feedback only when it is faithful to the source text. For unrelated non-legal text such as opening hours, entertainment, shopping, greetings, or casual chat, return the same schema with empty legal fields, is_legal_answer_required=false, is_standalone_question=true when the question is understandable, and exclusion_reason=non_legal_question.
